newsitem.title: SWEDEN: GOLF-HAEGGMAN WINS MASTERS AS GARRIDO EYES CUP SPOT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HAEGGMAN WINS MASTERS AS GARRIDO EYES CUP SPOT.

text.p: Joakim Haeggman of Sweden completed a runaway four-shot victory in the Scandinavian Masters on Sunday with his three-under-par final round of 69.
His 18-under-par total of 270 earned the Swede his second European Tour victory four years after his first, but much of the talk at Malmo concerned the Ryder Cup.

Spaniard Ignacio Garrido finished second to replace compatriot Jose Maria Olazabal in the 10th and last place in the Ryder Cup points table for automatic selection, with just three counting events left.
Irishman Padraig Harrington finished sixth to stay in 11th as Olazabal dropped to 12th.

European captain Severiano Ballesteros is hoping Olazabal will make it automatically to Valderrama so that he can use his two wild cards on Nick Faldo and Swede Jesper Parnevik, but his shared 38th place on Sunday did nothing to help that scenario.

Haeggman began the final round four ahead of the field and increased his lead until taking bogeys in the middle of his back-nine. But he finished with a flourish as his fifth birdie gave him a three-under-par round of 69.
The victory gave him an outside chance of his second Ryder Cup appearance following that in 1993 when he became the first Swede to play in the competition.
"The way I'm playing I can win again in the last three events," said Haeggman, who has moved up from 41st to 17th in the Cup table. "At least I have hope now.
"Four years was a long wait but I feel my game is back to the way it was in 1993, I'm focused again, too, so why not the Ryder Cup?"
Garrido's 67 for 274 included six birdies, three of them over the first four holes where he also ran up his only bogey by hitting into a hazard.
This left him one shot clear of another Swede, Mats Hallberg, and Peter Baker of England, with Welshman Mark Mouland a further stroke back and Harrington on 277 with Spaniard Jose Rivero.
If Garrido does make it into the Ryder Cup team he will follow in the footsteps of father Antonio, who partnered Ballesteros in the 1979 competition.
"My father will probably be far more excited and nervous about this than me," said a relaxed Garrido, who needed only 25 putts on his final round.
"I wasn't in the least bit nervous as I played today, even when I realised what second place was going to mean.
"I feel I can play good golf under pressure nowadays since I won in Germany and I think I am going to make it into the team. I have three events to go and just a couple of top-20s will get me in."
